name: Uzza
overview: Uzza was a male member of the tribe of Levi who served as a temple servant. His role as a temple servant indicates his involvement in the religious duties associated with the worship of the God of Israel. Scripture identifies him specifically in the context of the post-exilic community, emphasizing his Levitical heritage.
namesAndTitles: The name Uzza means "strong, fierce one," reflecting a characteristic of strength. This proper name was not given directly by God but is recorded in Ezra 2:49. The meaning of his name aligns with the qualities valued in those who served in the temple.
familyAndRelationships: Uzza is identified as a descendant of Levi, placing him within the Levitical lineage responsible for temple service. Beyond this tribal affiliation, Scripture does not provide additional details about his family relationships.
scriptureSignificance: Uzza's significance lies in his role as a temple servant from the tribe of Levi during the return from exile. His inclusion in the genealogical record in Ezra 2:49 highlights the continuity of the Levitical priestly and temple service line, which was crucial for the restoration of proper worship in Jerusalem. Through his service, Uzza contributed to the reestablishment of the covenant community centered on the worship of God.
